newsitem.title: USA: CME live, feeder cattle end weaker on cash concern.
newsitem.headline: CME live, feeder cattle end weaker on cash concern.

text.p: CME live and feeder cattle futures continued to slip late and closed weaker, with final values at or near day's lows on concern over the direction of cash cattle prices next week, traders said.

Live cattle closed 0.425 to 0.125 cent per lb lower with February off most at 63.550 cents and April off 0.300 at 65.625 cents. Feeder cattle finished 0.625 to 0.150 cent lower with March off most at 68.025 cents.

Live cattle retreated from a mixed trend early as concern grew over cash fed cattle markets next week. Packer bids will likely be down at least another $1 per cwt for cattle following recent weakness in beef, some sources said.
"The problem has been a pretty slack demand structure (for beef) the last three weeks or so," said Tom Tippens, CEO of Professional Cattle Consultants Inc.
Tippens noted that feedlots are trying to remain current and weights remain under year-ago levels, but sliding beef prices the past couple of weeks has kept packers cautious.

Boxed beef recently, had traded at the lowest levels since early May, before rising slightly Friday morning. Delivery concerns also prompted some liquidation in February futures as ahead of first notice day Monday, traders added.
